content:
incident-bot: Incident created: GPU serving cluster - repeated CUDA illegal memory access + container OOMs detected on serving-runtime. Severity: P2. Auto-alerting oncall.

Eve: seeing a cluster-wide spike of pod restarts on gpu-serving-prod, about 4 nodes. Errors are a mix of OOM and `CUDA illegal memory access` in the runtime container. App 5xx + latency up.

Jin: logs? stack traces? can you paste the tail of the pod logs and dmesg from one affected node?

Eve: pasted logs to the thread. snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA illegal memory access at 0x7fffb2f8. 2026-03-17T02:14:03Z Container exit code 139, kernel: BUG: bad pagetable in process <serving>```. Also saw repeated `pagemap: misaligned address` entries in dmesg.

Sam: ok. early hypothesis: a kernel driver/pagewalk race hitting our mmap path under eviction pressure. Could be triggered by recent kernel patch + high memory churn. Any recent node image changes?

Maria: customer impact: overall 5xx rate +3.2% in the last 12m; highest for acme-inc (approx 14% of their requests failing). Support already notified.

Lucas: mitigation plan proposal: 1) cordon + drain the 3 worst nodes to stop recurrence, 2) failover traffic to dedicated fallback pool (cpu/fallback models), 3) scale up CPU workers to absorb requests, 4) pin model variant (no quantization) for stability.

Eve: starting cordon on node-10 and node-12 now. Command: `kubectl cordon node-10 && kubectl drain node-10 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` :running:

ops-bot: node-10 cordoned, evicting pods (20 pods). node-12 cordon queued.

Jin: collecting `dmesg` from node-10: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=12345, Host: Illegal instruction / illegal memory access```. Also kernel trace shows `walk_pte()` warnings and `unaligned pagewalk` entries. This points to a race in the SMMU/pagetable path under heavy reclamation.

Sam: agree. while we triage kernel-level root cause, we should remove GPU pressure on affected nodes. Another quick mitigation: disable preemption for the container runtime or reduce per-pod GPU memory allocation via runtime config to reduce concurrent KV cache growth.

Maria: support update: telling acme-inc about degraded performance and failover to fallback pool. ETA for next customer update in 30m.

Lucas: I'm going to trigger routing policy change to send new requests to the dedicated fallback pool (cpu and small-gpu) and lower per-request concurrency for affected routes. Doing a canary switch: 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

Eve: canary flip started at 02:22Z. Observing reduced restarts on the cordoned nodes. 5xx trending down after 5m. :thumbsup:

Jin: collecting core dump from a crashed container for postmortem. Uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1700004321/core-node10.tar.gz. Added a note for kernel engineering.

Sam: long-term: we should test kernel repro with high eviction and large mmap workload, and consider a temporary kernel rollback for the affected instance pool if we can repro reliably. Also add runtime guard to reject suspicious large contiguous mmap that exceeds configured alignment checks.

ops-bot: routing policy updated: /v1/generate -> fallback-pool (50%) at 02:27Z, 100% at 02:34Z.

Maria: customers notified: acme-inc informed of mitigation and expected stabilization. Support ticket #INC-2026-0421 linked.

Eve: handoff to jin for continued triage and overnight coverage. I will stay available for 30m. Jin, take ownership please.

Jin: taking over. summary: cordoned 3 nodes (node-10,node-11,node-12), traffic rerouted to fallback pools, core dumps collected, customer notified. Next steps: run kernel repro, collaborate with kernel/drivers team, prepare hotfix or rollback. Will update every hour or on new findings. :eyes:

Lucas: adding postmortem owners: jin (lead), sam (runtime), lucas (routing), maria (customer comms).

Eve: thanks team. tagging incident-bot to generate incident record and timeline. :white_check_mark:
